brief: Use your own system or ClinicBook. You will produce a short architecture sketch that includes structure, decisions and task owners, without any special tooling.
do: List five to eight building blocks of your system, each with a one-sentence responsibility.
Draw or list the relations between the blocks, naming what flows along each relation.
Write two decision records of three to five lines each, with context, choice, one alternative and one consequence.
Name who currently does each architect task (clarify requirements, design, decide, communicate, check) and mark any task with no owner.
Pick one misconception from this lesson and describe where you saw it in your project.
done: Building blocks: Each block has a single clear responsibility and relations are named
Decisions: Records context, choice, an alternative and a consequence
Architect tasks: Maps every task to an owner and spots unowned tasks
Misconceptions: Finds a real example and states the correction
Evidence: The block list, the relations, two decision records, the task owner table, and one sentence on the misconception.
experienced: Apply it to a real system your team runs, with real numbers, real owners and real dates.
example:
**Blocks (ClinicBook):** Web App (patient and receptionist screens); Booking Service (rules for holding, moving and cancelling slots); Calendar Store (appointments and clinic calendars); Payment Adapter (talks to the payment provider); Reminder Adapter (talks to the messaging provider).

**Relations:** Web App asks Booking Service for slots; Booking Service reads and writes the Calendar Store; Booking Service sends deposit requests to Payment Adapter and reminder requests to Reminder Adapter.

**Decision 1.** Context: clinics are in several time zones. Choice: store appointment times in UTC plus the clinic time zone name. Alternative: store local time only. Consequence: conversion needed on every display, but no ambiguity.

**Decision 2.** Context: two people can pick the same slot. Choice: hold a slot for five minutes at selection. Alternative: check at confirmation only. Consequence: held slots look unavailable to others for a short time.

**Task owners:** requirements, product owner and lead developer; design, whole team; decisions, lead developer; communication, lead developer; checking against code, nobody yet (assign to one developer).

**Misconception seen:** "the framework is the architecture", when we picked a web framework before listing quality goals.
